from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

            FadeOut(prior_group),
            Create(universe_square),
            Write(universe_label)

        self.wait(3)
        
        # Reset colors for final wait
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(WHITE))
        self.wait(2)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Define lecture lines from storyboard
        title = "The Geometric Shift: Shrinking the Universe"
        lecture_lines = [
            "Observing evidence eliminates all 'no mound' possibilities.",
            "The remaining areas represent our narrowed-down reality.",
            "Now, the total probability space has significantly shrunk.",
            "We re-scale these remnants back into a full square.",
            "This physical transformation represents our updated belief."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title, lecture_lines)

        # Proportions for the geometric update
        p_bone = 0.4
        p_m_b = 0.8  # Likelihood of Mound given Bone
        p_m_nb = 0.2 # Likelihood of Mound given No Bone
        
        sq_size = 3.0
        
        # Grid boundaries derived from area B2 to E5
        origin_x = 1.5 # B2 center x
        origin_y = 1.2 # B2 center y
        
        # Calculate individual rectangle dimensions based on probabilities
        w_b = p_bone * sq_size
        w_nb = (1 - p_bone) * sq_size
        h_m_b = p_m_b * sq_size
        h_nm_b = (1 - p_m_b) * sq_size
        h_m_nb = p_m_nb * sq_size
        h_nm_nb = (1 - p_m_nb) * sq_size

        # Colors corresponding to storyboard descriptions
        color_a = "#5dade2" # Bone + Mound (Light Blue)
        color_b = "#aed6f1" # Bone + No Mound (Faded Blue)
        color_c = "#f5b041" # No Bone + Mound (Light Orange)
        color_d = "#fad7a0" # No Bone + No Mound (Faded Orange)
        color_gray = "#A9A9A9"

        # Create Rectangles representing initial state
        rect_a = Rectangle(width=w_b, height=h_m_b, fill_opacity=0.8, fill_color=color_a, stroke_width=2)
        rect_a.move_to([origin_x + w_b/2, origin_y - h_m_b/2, 0])
        
        rect_b = Rectangle(width=w_b, height=h_nm_b, fill_opacity=0.8, fill_color=color_b, stroke_width=2)
        rect_b.move_to([origin_x + w_b/2, origin_y - h_m_b - h_nm_b/2, 0])
        
        rect_c = Rectangle(width=w_nb, height=h_m_nb, fill_opacity=0.8, fill_color=color_c, stroke_width=2)
        rect_c.move_to([origin_x + w_b + w_nb/2, origin_y - h_m_nb/2, 0])
        
        rect_d = Rectangle(width=w_nb, height=h_nm_nb, fill_opacity=0.8, fill_color=color_d, stroke_width=2)
        rect_d.move_to([origin_x + w_b + w_nb/2, origin_y - h_m_nb - h_nm_nb/2, 0])

        # Labels for regions
        label_a = Text("Bone & Mound", font_size=12).move_to(rect_a)
        label_b = Text("Bone & No Mound", font_size=12).move_to(rect_b)
        label_c = Text("No Bone & Mound", font_size=12).move_to(rect_c)
        label_d = Text("No Bone & No Mound", font_size=12).move_to(rect_d)

        # Outer square outline container
        square_outline = Rectangle(width=sq_size, height=sq_size, color=WHITE, stroke_width=1)
        self.place_in_area(square_outline, "B2", "E5")

        self.add(rect_a, rect_b, rect_c, rect_d, label_a, label_b, label_c, label_d, square_outline)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Gray out regions that don't match the evidence ('No Mound')
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(color_gray))
        self.play(
            rect_b.animate.set_fill(color_gray),
            rect_d.animate.set_fill(color_gray),
            run_time=1
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Fade out the impossible regions
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE), self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(color_a))
        self.play(
            FadeOut(rect_b), FadeOut(rect_d),
            FadeOut(label_b), FadeOut(label_d),
            run_time=1
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Shift the remaining 'Mound' regions together to prepare for normalization
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(WHITE), self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        remaining_group = VGroup(rect_a, rect_c, label_a, label_c)
        self.play(
            remaining_group.animate.move_to(square_outline.get_center()),
            run_time=1
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # Re-scale the fragments to fill the original 1x1 probability space
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(WHITE), self.lecture[3].animate.set_color(GREEN))
        
        # Calculate normalization widths
        area_a = p_bone * p_m_b
        area_c = (1 - p_bone) * p_m_nb
        total_evidence_area = area_a + area_c
        
        new_w_a = (area_a / total_evidence_area) * sq_size
        new_w_c = (area_c / total_evidence_area) * sq_size
        
        # Target rectangles for transformation to full square
        final_rect_a = Rectangle(width=new_w_a, height=sq_size, fill_opacity=0.8, fill_color=color_a, stroke_width=2)
        final_rect_a.move_to(square_outline.get_center() + [-(sq_size - new_w_a)/2, 0, 0])
        
        final_rect_c = Rectangle(width=new_w_c, height=sq_size, fill_opacity=0.8, fill_color=color_c, stroke_width=2)
        final_rect_c.move_to(square_outline.get_center() + [(sq_size - new_w_c)/2, 0, 0])

        self.play(
            Transform(rect_a, final_rect_a),
            Transform(rect_c, final_rect_c),
            label_a.animate.move_to(final_rect_a.get_center()),
            label_c.animate.move_to(final_rect_c.get_center()),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        # Final label for the posterior probability

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # 1. Setup Layout
        title = "Bayes' Theorem & Geometry of Belief"
        lecture_lines = [
            "- Prior: Initial belief P(H)",
            "- Evidence: New data observed",
            "- Likelihood: P(E|H)",

        ]
        self.setup_layout(title, lecture_lines)

        formula = MathTex(

        posterior_box = SurroundingRectangle(likelihood_rect, color=YELLOW, buff=0.05)
        self.play(Create(posterior_box))
        
        post_text = Text("Posterior Focus", font_size=18, color=YELLOW)
        self.place_at_grid(post_text, "F3", scale_factor=1.0)
        self.play(Write(post_text))
        
        self.wait(3)

class Section6Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Summary: Belief as a Dynamic Shape", [
            "Probabilistic belief is a dynamic shape that shifts.",
            "Extraordinary claims require massive evidence to change this space.",
            "Use geometry to master the logic of uncertain worlds."
        ])

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Highlight Line 1
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(BLUE_C))

        # Dynamic Shape: A rectangle that morphs
        shape = Rectangle(width=2, height=2, color=BLUE_B, fill_opacity=0.5)
        self.place_in_area(shape, "C2", "E4")
        
        label_belief = Text("Belief Area", font_size=24, color=BLUE_B)
        self.place_at_grid(label_belief, "B3", scale_factor=0.8)

        self.play(DrawBorderThenFill(shape), Write(label_belief))
        self.wait(0.5)

        # Morphing the shape to show "dynamic"
        self.play(shape.animate.stretch_to_fit_width(1).stretch_to_fit_height(3), run_time=1)
        self.play(shape.animate.stretch_to_fit_width(3).stretch_to_fit_height(1), run_time=1)
        self.play(shape.animate.stretch_to_fit_width(2).stretch_to_fit_height(2), run_time=1)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Reset colors and highlight Line 2
        self.play(
            self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(GREEN_B)
        )

        # Extraordinary claim: Small Prior area
        new_label_prior = Text("Prior (Low Prob.)", font_size=24, color=RED_B)
        self.place_at_grid(new_label_prior, "B3", scale_factor=0.8)

        self.play(
            shape.animate.stretch_to_fit_width(0.2).set_color(RED_B),
            FadeTransform(label_belief, new_label_prior)
        )
        
        # Slider setup
        slider_line = Line(self.grid["F2"], self.grid["F5"], color=GREY)
        slider_label = Text("Evidence Strength (P(E|H))", font_size=20, color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(slider_label, "F3", scale_factor=0.8).shift(UP*0.5)
        
        tracker = ValueTracker(0.1)
        dot = Dot(color=GREEN_B)
        dot.add_updater(lambda d: d.move_to(slider_line.point_from_proportion(tracker.get_value())))
        
        evidence_box = Rectangle(width=0.2, height=0.1, color=GREEN_B, fill_opacity=0.3)
        # Use add_updater to keep the box aligned with the shape and scaled by the tracker
        evidence_box.add_updater(lambda b: b.match_x(shape).stretch_to_fit_height(tracker.get_value() * 3 + 0.1, about_edge=DOWN).align_to(shape, DOWN))

        self.add(slider_line, slider_label, dot, evidence_box)
        
        # Animate slider
        self.play(tracker.animate.set_value(0.5), run_time=1.5)
        self.wait(0.5)
        self.play(tracker.animate.set_value(0.9), run_time=1.5)
        
        # Show area growth significantly only at the end (the result of massive evidence)
        new_label_posterior = Text("Posterior", font_size=24, color=YELLOW_B)
        self.place_at_grid(new_label_posterior, "B3", scale_factor=0.8)

        self.play(
            shape.animate.stretch_to_fit_width(2.0).set_color(YELLOW_B),
            FadeTransform(new_label_prior, new_label_posterior),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Reset colors and highlight Line 3
        self.play(
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(GOLD_B)
        )

        # Final visual: Fade and transition to end
        all_visuals = VGroup(shape, new_label_posterior, slider_line, slider_label, dot, evidence_box)
        
        self.play(all_visuals.animate.scale(1.1).set_opacity(0.8), run_time=1.5)
        self.wait(2)
        
        # Fade out everything
        self.play(
            FadeOut(all_visuals),
            FadeOut(self.lecture),
            FadeOut(self.title)
        )
        self.wait(1)

outline.topic: Bayes' Theorem and the Geometry of Changing Probabilistic Beliefs
outline.target_audience: University students (STEM) and advanced high school students

sections.title: The Hook: The Detective's Dilemma
sections.content: Introduce the concept of 'updating beliefs' through a narrative. We start with an initial guess (Prior) and must adjust it when new evidence appears. Define the goal: To visualize how probability isn't just a number, but a physical space that shrinks and shifts.
sections.example: Detective 'Sherlock Bones' is looking for a hidden bone in a backyard. Initially, he thinks there is a 20% chance it is buried under the rose bushes (his 'Prior' belief).

sections.title: Prerequisite: Probability as Area
sections.content: Establish the geometric foundation. Represent the entire 'Universe of Possibilities' as a unit square with an area of 1. Any specific event is a sub-region (rectangle) within this square. The size of the area equals the probability of the event.
sections.example: Draw a 1x1 square. Color a vertical slice representing 20% of the width to show $P(Bone\ in\ Roses)$. The remaining 80% represents the bone being elsewhere.

sections.title: Introducing Evidence: The Likelihood Filter
sections.content: Introduce a new event (Evidence $E$). Show how this evidence overlaps with our prior belief. Explain $P(E|H)$—the probability of seeing evidence if our hypothesis is true—and $P(E|\neg H)$—the probability of seeing it if the hypothesis is false.
sections.example: Sherlock sees a 'mound of fresh dirt' ($E$). If the bone is there ($H$), there is a 90% chance of a mound. If the bone is NOT there ($\neg H$), there is still a 10% chance of a mound (maybe a mole did it). We draw these as horizontal slices across our vertical bars.

sections.title: The Geometric Shift: Shrinking the Universe
sections.content: This is the 'Bayesian Update.' Once evidence is observed, the parts of the square that do not match the evidence disappear. The 'Total Universe' is no longer the 1x1 square, but only the area where the evidence exists. We must 're-normalize' this new shape back into a full square to see our new probability.
sections.example: Visual: Grey out all areas of the square where there is 'No Mound.' We are left with two small rectangles: 'Bone + Mound' and 'No Bone + Mound.' We stretch these remaining pieces to fill a new 1x1 square.

sections.title: The Formal Equation: Mapping Geometry to Algebra
sections.content: Translate the visual stretching of areas into the formal Bayes' Theorem formula. Show that $P(H|E)$ is simply the ratio of the 'True Positive' area to the 'Total Evidence' area.
sections.example: Formula Overlay: $P(H|E) = \frac{P(E|H)P(H)}{P(E)}$. In our garden: $\frac{0.9 \times 0.2}{(0.9 \times 0.2) + (0.1 \times 0.8)}$. Calculation shows the probability jumped from 20% to ~69%.

sections.title: Summary: Belief as a Dynamic Shape
sections.content: Recap the transformation: Belief starts as a Prior area, is filtered by the Evidence area, and the result is the Posterior area. Emphasize that extraordinary claims (small prior area) require massive evidence (large likelihood ratio) to shift the geometry significantly.
sections.example: Animation: A slider showing that if the 'Mound' was very common everywhere, the 'Bone in Roses' area wouldn't grow much, visually demonstrating why weak evidence doesn't change minds.

storyboard.title: The Hook: The Detective's Dilemma
lecture_lines: Meet Sherlock Bones, a detective seeking hidden treasure.
He starts with an initial belief called a "Prior".
Visualizing probability as space makes updating beliefs intuitive.
animations: Show a cartoon detective 'Sherlock Bones' [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/detect.svg] looking at a backyard.
Display a bar labeled 'Prior Belief: 20%' in #FFD700 (Gold).
Shift the view to a large square representing the 'Universe of Possibilities'.

storyboard.title: Prerequisite: Probability as Area
lecture_lines: Imagine the entire universe of possibilities as a square.
The square's total area equals a probability of one.
Every specific event is a smaller rectangle inside it.
animations: Draw a white square #FFFFFF with side length 1, labeled 'Total Area = 1'.
Color a vertical slice (width 0.2) in #FFD700 (Gold), labeled 'Bone in Roses (20%)'.
Label the remaining area (width 0.8) in #A9A9A9 (Dark Gray) as 'Elsewhere (80%)'.

storyboard.title: Introducing Evidence: The Likelihood Filter
lecture_lines: A new clue appears: a mound of fresh dirt.
We must account for this evidence using a filter.
If the bone is there, a mound is likely.
If it is missing, a mound is still possible.
We draw these outcomes as horizontal slices of probability.
animations: Display the 'mound of fresh dirt' icon #8B4513 (Saddle Brown) at the top.
In the 'Bone in Roses' slice, color the top 90% in #32CD32 (Lime Green) labeled 'Mound | Bone'.
In the 'Elsewhere' slice, color the top 10% in #FF4500 (Orange Red) labeled 'Mound | No Bone'.
Highlight the horizontal line separating 'Mound' from 'No Mound'.
Fade the labels slightly to show the intersection areas clearly.

storyboard.title: The Geometric Shift: Shrinking the Universe
lecture_lines: Observing evidence eliminates all "no mound" possibilities.
The remaining areas represent our narrowed-down reality.
Now, the total probability space has significantly shrunk.
We re-scale these remnants back into a full square.
This physical transformation represents our updated belief.
animations: Gray out #A9A9A9 all areas labeled 'No Mound'.
Fade out the grayed-out regions, leaving only the 'Mound' rectangles.
Shift the 'Mound | Bone' and 'Mound | No Bone' rectangles together.
Scale (stretch) the combined rectangles to fill the original 1x1 square dimensions.
Label the new width of the 'Bone' section as the 'Posterior Probability'.

storyboard.title: The Formal Equation: Mapping Geometry to Algebra
lecture_lines: Let’s translate this visual stretching into a formal equation.
Bayes' Theorem calculates the ratio of these specific areas.
The numerator is the "True Positive" region we kept.
The denominator is the total area of the evidence.
Algebra confirms what our geometry just demonstrated.
animations: Fade in the formula P(H|E) = [P(E|H)P(H)] / P(E) in #FFFFFF.
Highlight P(E|H)P(H) and point it to the 'Bone + Mound' rectangle using [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/bone.svg].
Highlight P(E) and point it to the total 'Mound' area.
Show the numbers being plugged in: 0.18 / (0.18 + 0.08).
Display the result: 69%, showing the 'Bone' area [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/bone.svg] has significantly grown.

storyboard.title: Summary: Belief as a Dynamic Shape
lecture_lines: Probabilistic belief is a dynamic shape that shifts.
Extraordinary claims require massive evidence to change this space.
Use geometry to master the logic of uncertain worlds.
animations: Show a quick replay of the area shrinking and stretching.
Display a slider [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/slider.svg] that adjusts the 'Mound frequency' [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/m.svg] (P(E|~H)).
Demonstrate that if P(E|~H) is high, the area doesn't change much, then fade to black.
